findings.message: The criteria require the journal-backed producer to be bound to the production Box enqueue path so that every new and deduped arrival reports. On main, squatch/__main__.py builds no Box. Production Box instances are built inside squatch/runner.py (lines 288 and 347), squatch/stages.py (line 513), squatch/merge.py (line 172), squatch/triage.py (line 173) and squatch/author.py (line 145). Each takes only state_dir, fs and clock, with no journal or producer. Box cannot open its own Journal because the journal has a single writer that holds the lock. So activating the producer through the __main__.py root forces edits to these construction sites, and none of them is in the fence or in Context.
findings.paved_road: Add every production Box construction site that must carry the bound producer to both Scope fence and Context: at least squatch/runner.py, squatch/stages.py and squatch/merge.py, plus squatch/triage.py and squatch/author.py if their enqueues count as arrivals. Add their existing tests as fenced or preservation suites. Alternatively, state the exact Box/daemon seam from the storm-producer-wiring contract that lets __main__.py inject the producer without touching those modules, and cite where it is threaded.

findings.message: Scope in and the criteria say 'the same production Box instance', but production builds several independent Box instances (runner, stages, merge, triage, author). A test can bind one instance while arrivals through the others stay unobserved. That makes 'reports every new and signature-deduped arrival' unprovable as written, and it lets daemon-only or partial activation pass.
findings.paved_road: Restate the criterion as: every production Box construction reachable from the squatch/__main__.py drain/run composition (name each one) is bound to the one journal-backed producer. Have tests/test_storm_notification_activation.py prove this for at least the harvest/second-problem path and the verification-attribution failure_report path.
